content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 吉利德收购瀚辰星泰口服IL-23R抑制剂HCXT-2001，I期国产大环肽创新药实现重磅出海 吉利德收购瀚辰星泰口服IL-23R抑制剂HCXT-2001，I期国产大环肽创新药实现重磅出海 李明轩 · 医药投融资分析师 李 李明轩 医药投融资分析师 审核：孙浩 · 特许金融分析师（CFA） 聚焦创新药投融资、小核酸药物与代谢疾病赛道；长期跟踪国内 Biotech 融资动态与管线进展。累计发布原创分析 200+ 篇。 19小时前 1137 吉利德科学 瀚辰星泰 HCXT-2001 IL-23R 企业收购 近日（10月22日），吉利德科学宣布，已与瀚辰星泰（PepStar Therapeutics Limited）达成最终协议，将收购其口服IL-23R抑制剂项目，包括核心资产HCXT-2001，首付款为12.75亿美元。图源：吉利德官网值得关注的是，HCXT-2001目前仍处于Ⅰ期临床阶段。高额首付款与早期临床开发阶段形成鲜明反差，也让这款国产创新药及其背后的口服IL-23R赛道受到关注。一、12.75亿美元首付款，押注口服IL-23RHCXT-2001是一款处于临床开发阶段的口服大环肽IL-23R抑制剂，具有延长半衰期的设计特点，旨在为口服IL-23通路抑制提供潜在的差异化方案。IL-23R是免疫介导的炎症性疾病领域的临床验证靶点，相关药物在炎症性肠病（IBD）、银屑病等疾病领域具有开发潜力。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此次交易将使吉利德获得相关IL-23R抑制剂项目的全球权益，进一步丰富其炎症与免疫学产品组合。对于仍处于Ⅰ期临床阶段的HCXT-2001而言，12.75亿美元首付款无疑是此次交易最受关注的看点。不过，交易金额体现的是买方对相关资产及其潜在价值的判断，并不意味着产品的临床疗效已经得到验证。二、口服IL-23R赛道升温，国内药企加速布局口服IL-23R抑制剂正成为免疫炎症领域值得关注的研发方向。目前，强生的口服环肽IL-23R抑制剂 icotrokinra（JNJ-2113）已获批上市，为这一靶点的口服药物开发提供了重要进展。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库国内企业也在推进相关布局。今年7月，翰森制药将口服IL-23R抑制剂HS-20118的相关全球权益授权给Avere Therapeutics。根据翰森制药公告，该交易包括1.2亿美元首付款、最高21.8亿美元里程碑付款，以及未来销售提成；翰森制药同时参与了Avere的融资。图源：翰森制药企业公告此外，信立泰、海思科、海量医药、诺诚健华等国内企业也在相关方向有所布局。从口服给药到半衰期优化，相关产品正探索不同的研发路径。不过，各产品在分子设计、临床数据及开发进度上存在差异，后续竞争仍需回归疗效、安全性与给药便利性等关键维度。三、高额交易背后，国产创新药资产受关注吉利德此次收购，将市场关注点再次引向国产创新药的海外交易价值。对于HCXT-2001而言，目前仍处于Ⅰ期临床阶段，后续能否在临床研究中验证其安全性、疗效及长效化设计的潜在价值，仍有待进一步观察。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库与此同时，口服IL-23R抑制剂领域已有产品获批上市，国内多家药企也在推进相关研发。随着赛道持续发展，分子设计、临床开发和差异化竞争能力，将成为影响产品后续价值的重要因素。12.75亿美元首付款为此次交易带来足够的关注度，但对于一款早期临床资产而言，真正的考验仍在后续研发。参考来源：[1] title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. Neither release addresses market reaction, and independent verification of the platform’s performance in these indications was not available at the time of publication.SourcesAstraZeneca announces new strategic collaboration with insitro to use advanced AI systems to develop transformative therapeutics for difficult to treat cardiometabolic diseases. MADRID — A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of disease recurrence in patients with melanoma by 42% compared to a standard treatment, according to a large clinical trial conducted by the drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The results are an important advance for the treatment of melanoma, oncologists said, because patients lived significantly longer without their cancer returning. content: STAT PlusBiotech AbbVie skin disorder drug succeeds in late-stage trial, but results miss market expectations Findings dim hopes lutikizumab can compete with UCB’s Bimzelx Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Jonathan WosenOct. 22, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. AbbVie reported on Thursday that an experimental therapy for hidradenitis suppurativa, a chronic skin condition, succeeded in a late-stage trial but missed market expectations, leaving experts doubtful the drug can compete with the current standard of care. In the Phase 3 Intrepid trial, which enrolled 1,400 patients with moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa, 31.4% of participants given weekly injections of AbbVie’s therapy, lutikizumab, reported a 75% or greater reduction in the number of inflamed bumps and abscesses across their skin, compared to 23.4% of those in the placebo group after 16 weeks. This measure was the study’s primary endpoint.Advertisement The company also reported that the drug met eight secondary endpoints, including improvements in skin pain and flares. Lutikizumab was generally safe and well tolerated, with adverse event rates that were nearly identical between the placebo and treatment groups. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? 10月22日，国家药监局官网显示，石药集团/和铂医药申报的进口1类新药巴托利单抗注射液获批上市，用于治疗全身型重症肌无力（gMG）。图源：NMPA官网一、历经两次上市申报，巴托利单抗终于获批巴托利单抗（HBM9161）是一款全人源抗新生儿Fc受体（FcRn）单克隆抗体，可阻断FcRn与免疫球蛋白G（IgG）结合，加速体内IgG清除，从而减少致病性IgG介导的自身免疫反应。在全身型重症肌无力III期临床研究中，巴托利单抗取得积极结果。2021年1月，该药被CDE纳入突破性治疗药物程序。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库巴托利单抗的权益合作始于2017年9月。当时，和铂医药从HanAll Biopharma获得包括巴托利单抗在内的两款创新生物制品在中国（包括香港、澳门和台湾）的开发、生产及商业化权益。2022年10月，和铂医药与石药集团全资子公司恩必普药业有限公司达成合作协议，在中国共同开发巴托利单抗。其中，和铂医药负责该药针对全身型重症肌无力的完整临床试验设计与执行，并根据产品年度净销售额获得分层销售提成。在上市申报方面，巴托利单抗注射液于2023年6月首次获NMPA受理，受理号为JXSS2300049。此后，因III期临床试验延期，相关申请被主动撤回。2024年7月，相关方重新递交上市申请，受理号为JXSS2400060。历经两年多审评，该药终于于2026年10月获批上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库二、FcRn靶点已有多款药物获批，市场竞争持续近年来，FcRn抑制剂逐步成为全身型重症肌无力治疗领域的重要研发方向，国内已有多款相关药物获批。2023年7月，Argenx与再鼎医药合作开发的艾加莫德α获批进口。2025年3月，优时比的罗泽利昔珠单抗获批进口。该药是全球首个同时覆盖乙酰胆碱受体（AChR）抗体阳性和肌肉特异性酪氨酸激酶（MuSK）抗体阳性全身型重症肌无力患者的FcRn抑制剂。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库随着巴托利单抗获批，国内全身型重症肌无力治疗领域再添一款FcRn靶向药物。后续其临床应用及市场表现，值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] title: FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction for Skyrizi in Crohn's Disease
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 23, 2026 FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction for Skyrizi in Crohn's Disease Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff FDA approved an at-home induction option for risankizumab-rzaa in adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease, based on the phase 3 AFFIRM trial. Advertisement The FDA today approved a subcutaneous induction regimen for AbbVie's Skyrizi (risankizumab-rzaa) in adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.1 The decision lets patients start treatment at home with an on-body injector (OBI) induction pack instead of an intravenous infusion, and continue with the same device during maintenance.1AbbVie filed for the new regimen April 27 and had said it anticipated approval later in 2026.2 The decision changes how therapy begins, not who is eligible, because intravenous induction remains an option.1 "People living with Crohn's disease need treatments that can deliver meaningful disease control from the start," said Roopal Thakkar, M.D., executive vice president, research and development, chief scientific officer, AbbVie. "With the approval of subcutaneous induction, we are building on the strong efficacy of Skyrizi while giving patients and physicians greater flexibility in how treatment is initiated. This is one more example of how AbbVie continues to advance treatment to better meet the needs of people living with Crohn's disease."Key FactsDrug: risankizumab-rzaa; interleukin-23 inhibitorIndication: Moderate-to-severe Crohn's, adultsAction: FDA approves subcutaneous inductionTrial: Phase 3 AFFIRM, 274 patients, randomized 2:1Week 12 clinical remission: 56% vs 30%Week 12 endoscopic response: 43% vs 15%Safety: No new risks (company-reported)Status: U.S. approval, Oct. 23, 2026What does the new induction regimen involve?The subcutaneous regimen is 720 mg delivered by the OBI induction pack at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 8.1 Patients can still begin intravenously with 600 mg at weeks 0, 4 and 8. Either way, maintenance dosing starts at week 12 and is given by OBI every eight weeks.1 The device was first introduced in 2022 for Crohn's disease maintenance.1Lead investigator Millie D. Long, M.D., of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, said: "When patients and I discuss treatment, they want to know two things: will it work? And how will it fit into their lives? AFFIRM answered the first question, with superior rates of clinical remission and endoscopic response versus placebo during induction with subcutaneous Skyrizi, particularly in patients new to advanced therapy. This approval answers the second. As a physician who has used the Skyrizi OBI, I've seen firsthand the convenience it can offer patients. Now with this approval, patients can start treatment at home and continue the same way through maintenance."What did the phase 3 AFFIRM trial show?AFFIRM randomly assigned 274 adults 2:1 to subcutaneous risankizumab or placebo, and 65% had previously failed advanced therapy.1 The co-primary endpoints at week 12 were clinical remission, defined as a Crohn's disease activity index score below 150, and endoscopic response.1 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); In the total population, 56% of treated patients reached clinical remission versus 30% with placebo, and 43% had an endoscopic response versus 15% (both p<0.001).1 Endoscopic remission, a secondary endpoint, occurred in 26% versus 11%.1Results were stronger in patients without prior advanced therapy failure: 74% versus 27% for clinical remission and 60% versus 15% for endoscopic response. In patients who had failed advanced therapy, the rates were 45% versus 31% and 33% versus 15%.1 AbbVie reported no new safety risks.1How does this fit with earlier risankizumab data?Skyrizi is an interleukin-23 inhibitor that binds the p19 subunit and is also approved for ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.1 In Crohn's disease, the earlier phase 3 ADVANCE and MOTIVATE trials tested intravenous induction. Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 45% of patients receiving 600 mg versus 25% with placebo in ADVANCE, and 42% versus 20% in MOTIVATE.3 The trials enrolled different populations, so those figures cannot be compared directly with AFFIRM.Why does Crohn's disease remain a treatment challenge?Crohn's disease is a chronic, progressive condition that most often affects the area between the small intestine and colon, causing persistent diarrhea and abdominal pain, and it can lead to complications or surgery.1 In AFFIRM, advanced therapy referred to biologics or Janus kinase inhibitors, and the 65% prior-failure rate reflects how many participants had already tried earlier treatment without adequate results.1 What are the limitations and next steps?The advanced therapy-naive subgroup was small, with 65 treated and 33 placebo patients, and the p-values AbbVie reported apply to the total population rather than subgroups.1 The company's description of the results as market-leading is a comparative claim, and the release includes no head-to-head data to support it. Results from AFFIRM's extension periods were not reported in the announcement, and the safety conclusion rests on the sponsor's summary.1FDA also approved revised prescribing information across all indications, advising clinicians to consider tuberculosis evaluation based on clinical judgment; no test is mandatory before treatment.1 Liver monitoring guidance for Crohn's disease remains in the label.1SourcesAbbVie. title: Bristol Myers Squibb Discloses Patient Death in CAR-T Multiple Sclerosis Trial
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 26, 2026 Bristol Myers Squibb Discloses Patient Death in CAR-T Multiple Sclerosis Trial Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Bristol Myers Squibb discloses results from it's Phase I Breakfree-2 trial of CAR-T therapy zola-cel for multiple sclerosis. Advertisement Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) has disclosed a patient death in its early-stage Breakfree-2 trial studying zolacabtagene autoleucel, an investigational, autologous CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy, in patients with relapsing or progressive forms of multiple sclerosis (MS).The death was disclosed as part of a broader data readout presented in an oral presentation at MSToronto 2026 and follows the company’s decision to place a voluntary pause on zola-cel studies back in September.What happened to the patient?The patient, who had highly active relapsing MS, died of septic pneumonia one day after receiving high-dose chemotherapy and 44 days after zola-cel infusion.1 According to BMS, the patient experienced late-onset, non-ICANS motor symptoms following infusion that did not resolve with intermittent corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin.Although the patient’s CAR-T cell expansion was consistent with that observed across the study, physicians administered high-dose cyclophosphamide, after which the patient developed septic pneumonia and died the following day. A BMS spokesperson told Reuters, “The patient had a late onset side effect, a series of other complications and was heavily pretreated prior to CAR T, confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”2 BMS says the death was unrelated to the earlier voluntary pause and that no additional Grade 5 events have occurred across any zola-cel autoimmune disease program, which has treated 190 patients in Phase I studies to date. 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 18小时前 1016 康方生物 依沃西单抗注射液 优先审评 胆道癌 新适应症 10月23日，CDE官网公示，康方生物的依沃西单抗注射液一项新适应症拟纳入优先审评，拟用于联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。图源：CDE官网此次申报进展与Ⅲ期临床研究HARMONi-GI1取得积极结果有关。2026年8月，康方生物宣布，该研究在预设期中分析中达到总生存期（OS）主要终点，并达到无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）的全部关键次要终点。一、胆道癌Ⅲ期研究取得阳性结果依沃西单抗是康方生物自主研发的PD-1/VEGF双特异性抗体，也是全球首创的PD-1/VEGF双特异性肿瘤免疫治疗药物。摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，2024年该品种在中国首次上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库本次拟纳入优先审评的新适应症为依沃西单抗联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。在Ⅲ期临床研究AK112-309/HARMONi-GI1中，研究人员采用随机、双盲、对照、多中心设计，评估依沃西单抗联合化疗与度伐利尤单抗联合化疗一线治疗晚期胆道恶性肿瘤的疗效与安全性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2026年8月，康方生物宣布，经独立数据监察委员会（IDMC）评估的预设期中分析显示，HARMONi-GI1研究达到OS主要终点，结果具有统计学显著性；同时达到PFS和ORR的全部关键次要终点。康方生物在新闻稿中表示，度伐利尤单抗联合化疗是国内外指南共同推荐的一线标准治疗方案（SOC）。公司称，HARMONi-GI1是胆道癌领域首个以PD-L1单抗联合化疗为对照、取得OS显著阳性结果的Ⅲ期研究。该研究结果已入选2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）大会突破性摘要（LBA8，主席论坛），康方生物将于大会首次披露具体研究数据。二、依沃西单抗持续拓展适应症目前，依沃西单抗已在中国获批三项适应症，覆盖EGFR-TKI耐药的非鳞状非小细胞肺癌（nsq-NSCLC）、PD-L1阳性非小细胞肺癌一线治疗及鳞状非小细胞肺癌一线治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库除国内市场外，依沃西单抗也在推进海外商业化。2022年12月，康方生物将依沃西单抗部分海外权益授权给美国Summit Therapeutics，交易方案包括50亿美元以上的潜在付款及两位数百分比的销售提成。目前，依沃西单抗联合化疗用于第三代EGFR-TKI治疗后进展的EGFR突变非鳞状非小细胞肺癌的美国上市申请正在审评中。此次胆道癌新适应症拟纳入优先审评，意味着依沃西单抗在肺癌之外进一步拓展实体瘤治疗领域。后续研究具体数据及审评进展，值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] CDE官网[2] title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on global sales.What is insitro’s platform?Insitro’s Virtual Human platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. In a statement, Caribou CEO Rachel Haurwitz said the current financing environment has made it “increasingly challenging” to secure the money needed to advance the company’s two main research programs, which focus on a hard-to-make form of medicine known as “off-the-shelf” cell therapy. As such, Caribou has made the “difficult decision” not to further develop its programs and to “evaluate strategic alternatives” — common corporate lingo for opening itself up to various deals. Caribou’s board of directors has already cleared management to start evaluating a potential merger, acquisition, business combination or other transactions. The company has also tapped Wedbush Securities to serve as its exclusive financial advisor in this process. To Daina Graybosch, an analyst at Leerink Partners who covers Caribou, the natural end for the company now is either a reverse merger or an acquisition by Tang Capital, a San Diego-based investment firm that made a name for itself by buying up cash-rich biotechs and returning much of their value to shareholders. Caribou ended the second quarter with $114 million worth of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. “I think Rachel and the team really do believe in their assets, but it's a real struggle,” Graybosch said. “And when you finally do raise [capital], it just gets more and more dilutive. It trades on the Nasdaq, for example, which is more attractive to private drug developers than lower-tier, over-the-counter markets. A researcher works in Caribou's labs, where the company was designing cell therapies for blood malignancies. Permission granted by Caribou Biosciences Caribou may also have a subzero enterprise value, which, in broad strokes, means that after accounting for its cash pile, the market is attributing nothing — or, really, less than nothing — to the company’s core operating business. That can actually be a plus to private developers, as it signals they might not have to pay a big premium to snag the public vehicle. Using its June 30 financials and closing share price Wednesday, Caribou would have a negative enterprise value of roughly $20 million. (Notably, that’s at the low end of a range from Leerink, which estimates the figure could be as much as $30 million depending on how much cash Caribou spent in the third quarter.) “I would definitely say a reverse merger is on the table here,” said Emmett Sweeney, a vice president on the healthcare investment banking team at Raymond James. Perhaps what makes Caribou such an obvious reverse merger prospect is it publicly stating that it’s exploring strategic alternatives. When companies do that, they become “low-hanging fruit” for reverse merger deals, according to David Kellman, a managing director and head of life sciences and biopharma investment banking at Citizens. They’re “basically running auction processes” with private companies, Kellman said in an interview earlier this month. “Those are the most obvious candidates, regardless of other criteria.” Caribou’s statement, including the mention of Wedbush being its strategic advisor, is a sign that company leaders are “serious” and “mean business,” Sweeney said. Clearly, “they want to move quickly. That's another aspect of Caribou that makes it an attractive merger partner.” Sweeney and others anticipate that Caribou, if not already, will soon be inundated with inbounds from private companies interested in merging. With roughly two dozen biotech reverse mergers announced this year, “the question for many companies is no longer whether the structure works, but whether they can find the right shell and execute the transaction on attractive terms,” Raymond James analysts wrote in a note to clients Wednesday. One lingering question is whether Caribou’s now-discontinued drugs will find a new home. Graybosch doesn’t have high hopes — in part because of rival programs advancing at other cell therapy developers like Fate Therapeutics and AvenCell Therapeutics, both of which are backed by major life sciences investors and large pharmaceutical firms. “Very rarely do these assets show up [again],” she said. “If I'm an investor thinking, ‘Do I wrap a new company around this asset, or do I go invest in AvenCell or Fate,’ I probably choose AvenCell or Fate at this point.” Recommended Reading A booming business on Wall Street would love more biotechs to quietly die By Jacob Bell • Sept. 10, 2026 Add us on Google Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Filed Under: Deals

As early evidence of the drugs’ promise emerges, and personal stories circulate on social media platforms, some patients have explicitly sought out the drugs to cut down on drinking.
